title: Beyond Rephrasing: Book-Level Organization Improves Synthetic Textbook Data for Mid-Training
abstract: arXiv:2607.28109v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Synthetic textbook data has improved language model pre-training, but prior work largely treats the benefit as a property of generated content or local rewriting style. We study a different factor: whether related content is organized into coherent book-level documents. We contribute both a scalable synthesis pipeline and controlled evidence that this organization matters. The pipeline retrieves source material from a pre-training corpus, clusters it into topical units, plans hierarchical tables of contents, and assembles source-grounded sections into complete books (our Full setting), yielding 686K textbooks (32B tokens) across 15,000+ disciplines. Replacing natural books in a mid-training mix with this corpus improves downstream performance by +1.09 on average. Controlled comparisons then disentangle the relevant design factors. translated_title: 超越改写：书籍级组织结构提升用于中期训练的合成教科书数据
translated_abstract: 合成教科书数据已经改善了语言模型的预训练，但以往的工作大多将这种收益视为生成内容本身或局部改写风格的属性。我们研究了一个不同的因素：相关内容是否被组织成连贯的书籍级文档。我们既贡献了一条可扩展的合成流水线，也提供了受控证据证明这种组织方式确实重要。该流水线从预训练语料库中检索源材料，将其聚类为主题单元，规划层次化的目录，并将有源依据的章节组装成完整的书籍（即我们的Full设置），在15,000多个学科中产出了68.6万本教科书（320亿词元）。在中期训练的数据混合中用该语料库替换自然书籍，可使下游性能平均提升+1.09。随后通过受控比较来分离相关的设计因素：内容匹配的Split设置保持生成的文本和词元完全不变，但将每个章节作为独立的……（摘要原文在此处被截断）
tldr: 该论文的核心发现是，合成教科书数据收益的关键不在于生成内容或改写风格，而在于将相关内容组织成连贯的书籍级文档——其提出的可扩展流水线（检索、聚类、目录规划、组装成书）生成了68.6万本有源依据的教科书（320亿词元），在中期训练中替换自然书籍可使下游性能平均提升+1.09。
en_tdlr: This paper demonstrates that book-level organization, rather than generated content or local rewriting style, is the key factor behind synthetic textbook data's benefits: a scalable pipeline that assembles 686K source-grounded textbooks (32B tokens) improves mid-training downstream performance by +1.09 on average when replacing natural books.
